This vegetation describes plants growth and development
Green Color : represents dense and more developed plants.
Orange Color : represents less-developed plants vegetation fraction.
Red Color : Indicates bare soil or sparse vegetation.
<div><strong>Green Color :</strong> indi:

<div>This map is to determine the nitrog:
This map is to determine the nitrogen content of the crops in the field, agnostic of the content that’s in the soil.
Red : soil.
Orange : unhealthy plants.
Green :healthy plants Healthy vegetation with high nitrogen content typically exhibits high chlorophyll content.
<div><strong>Green :</strong> High value:
Green : High values indicate healthy vegetation.
Red : low values indicate stressed vegetation, non-vegetated areas, or areas with low vegetation density.
<div>The Normalized Difference Moisture:
The Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) is a vegetation index used to assess soil moisture content.
Green Color : Indicates higher soil moisture content.
Reddish Color : Indicates lower soil moisture content.
<div>The Plant Senescence Reflectance In:
The Plant Senescence Reflectance Index (PSRI) is a vegetation index used to assess the senescence or aging of plants. It provides insights into the health and vitality of vegetation, particularly during later stages of growth.
Reddish Color : Indicates areas with higher senescence or aging in vegetation.
Green Color : Represents healthier and less senescent vegetation.
PSRI is valuable for monitoring plant stress, identifying areas with declining health, and optimizing agricultural management.
